summary: Report the state root's repo-relative path on TickContext, so a promptArgs hook reads it instead of recomputing it from a repoRoot it was never given.
tests: a dispatcher-built TickContext carries the state root's path relative to the repo root
build's per-tick args name the entry's note path from the tick context alone
pins: build's per-tick args refuse a state root outside the repo rather than naming a note path no commit holds
acceptance: buildPromptArgs takes only the declaration and the tick context, and computeStateRootRel has no caller under harness/.
notes: GateContext already carries this fact (*What a gate receives*); TickContext does not, so harness/prompts.ts takes repoRoot and re-runs computeStateRootRel. A fanout tick's cwd is the worktree and flumeDir is not nested under repoRoot, so no hook can derive it. Blocks HARNESS-PHASES: the factory has no repoRoot to pass. The section's TickContext bullet gains a row — spec is the human's.

summary: Ship flume-harness, the bin the package carries beside the engine's flume, and its init verb: the declaration skeleton, the state root, the ignore set and PROTOCOL.md.
tests: flume-harness init writes a declaration.ts skeleton the package's schema parses
flume-harness init writes the state root and its derived ignore lines
flume-harness init writes PROTOCOL.md from the package's own template
flume-harness init refuses a state root that already exists rather than overwriting it
pins: the engine's flume bin exposes no harness verb
acceptance: node bin/flume-harness.js init in an empty repo writes a declaration the package's schema parses, the state root, the ignore set and PROTOCOL.md.
notes: The shim is bin/flume.js's shape — argv through, stdio inherited, exit code out, no options of its own (spec/cli.md, *Distribution*). The files allowlist must cover the template: tsc emits no .md into dist/, and CI asserts the packed set both ways. The skeleton is a TypeScript module (*What a consumer declares*), so it cannot sit under harness/ as a .ts file — tsc would compile it. The engine's verb set stays closed; that is why the verb lives here.

summary: Add the package's chain factory: a complete Chain from one declaration — three plan slices and the fanout build phase, each with its prompt, gates and handoff.
tests: the factory returns the three plan slices and the build phase from a declaration
a plan slice the declaration does not enable is absent from the returned chain
the returned build phase is fanout and carries the declaration's fence
each returned phase names its prompt by an absolute path the package ships
the factory passes the declared supervisor policy to the chain whole
every placeholder the package's prompts name is supplied by the phase the factory returns for it
each returned phase runs the handoff the declaration names for it, else the package's default
acceptance: harness/chain.ts turns a parsed declaration into a Chain whose phases, prompts, gates and handoff are the package's.
notes: The assembly point: it wires the gates, the judge, the handoff, the windows, the prompt args and the entry extension, and carries setup, agents and slots through. .flume/chain.ts becomes this factory over .flume/declaration.ts at the cutover — an interactive chore(flume):, never build's (the cutover ruling, 6286ba8). Declared data keys and the gate verdict field are ratified (3572fe5) and land before that cutover, not here.
